title: How To Close Your Trade In Pieces Using TradingView and book Partial Profit or Loss
description:
Here I will show you How To Close Your Trade In Pieces Using TradingView and book Partial Profit or Loss 

In this video, I'll show you how to close your trade in pieces using TradingView, a vital skill for traders seeking more control over their positions. Whether you aim to lock in profits gradually or mitigate risks, this tutorial will guide you through the process step by step.

Start by visiting TradingView's homepage. If you haven't already, log into your account—it's quick and straightforward to set up. Once logged in, head to the chart section where your trading setup is displayed. This area provides a visual representation of market data and allows you to interact directly with your trades.

To begin closing a trade in pieces, locate the position you want to manage on the chart. Look for the ""close position"" button, which lets you modify your open trades. Clicking this button is essential, especially if you have multiple positions open, to avoid any confusion.

Next, explore the options for closing a portion of your trade. After selecting ""close position,"" you'll see an option for a partial close. This feature lets you specify how much of the position you want to close, leaving the rest open. It's particularly useful for capturing some profits while keeping part of the trade running for potentially higher gains.

Once you've decided on the portion to close, you'll find a checkbox or dropdown menu labeled ""partial close option."" Ensure you select this option, as it differentiates between closing the entire position and closing part of it. After confirming your partial close, enter the exact amount or percentage of the trade you wish to close. This step allows you to fine-tune the trade size, aligning it with your risk management strategy.

Once you're satisfied with your entries, click ""close"" to proceed. You've successfully closed your trade in pieces on TradingView. This method offers flexibility, enabling you to control how much of your position is closed at any given time, effectively managing your risk and reward ratio.

By following each step closely, you've now mastered how to close trades in segments. Remember, the key to proficiency is practice and understanding how each component works together. Thank you for watching, and happy trading!"

title: How to share your Chart on TradingView 2026 in form of Image, Tweet Link, Download Easily
description:
Here I will show you How to share your Chart on TradingView 2026 in form of Image, Tweet Link, Download Easily.


In this video, I'll guide you on how to share your chart setup on TradingView. If you're eager to share your insights or the trading setups you've crafted, TradingView makes it incredibly straightforward. Let's dive into the process so you can get started immediately.

First, head over to tradingview.com. Sign into your account, or if you don't have one yet, quickly sign up—it's a fast process. Once logged in, navigate to the chart section by clicking on ""Chart"" in the top menu. This is where you'll work with all your data and visualizations that you want to share.

Now, with your chart displayed and ready, focus on the upper right corner of the screen. You'll find a small camera icon there—your gateway to sharing your chart setup in multiple ways. Click on the camera icon to explore your sharing options.

If you want to share your chart as a downloadable image, click on the ""Download Image"" button. This allows you to save an image file of your chart directly onto your device. You can then easily attach it to an email, embed it in a presentation, or upload it to your favorite social media platforms.

Alternatively, if you prefer not to save the file but still want to share the image, TradingView offers a ""Copy Image"" option. Clicking this copies the chart image to your clipboard, enabling you to paste it directly into a document or chat message. This makes it seamless when sharing across platforms that support pasting from the clipboard.

Suppose you'd rather share a link to your chart instead of the image itself. TradingView simplifies this with a direct link option. After clicking the camera icon, you can copy a direct link to your chart setup, allowing others to view it online. This is particularly useful for sharing real-time data with someone who wants to see the chart in the same interactive format you've created.

Lastly, if you're an active Twitter user, you'll appreciate TradingView's social sharing integration. You can tweet the image directly from the platform. Simply click ""Tweet Image,"" craft a short message, and bring your followers directly to your insights in their Twitter feed.

As you can see, sharing your TradingView setups is straightforward. Whether through an image, a direct link, or a tweet, TradingView offers flexible options tailored to your sharing needs. Thanks for tuning in, and happy trading!"
